Q0155

“Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the way…” — The Doctrine of the Mean (Liji, Zhongyong)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Liji, Zhongyong. Theme: sincerity.

Quotes / The Doctrine of the Mean / Q0155

English

Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the way of human beings.
Thinker The Doctrine of the Mean
School Confucianism
Source Liji, Zhongyong
Theme Sincerity

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Liji, Zhongyong and files it under Confucianism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About The Doctrine of the Mean

The Doctrine of the Mean appears in this archive through verified English quotations associated with the Confucianism tradition. Biographical certainty varies by figure and text; where the “author” is a scripture or school anthology, read the name as a traditional attribution rather than a modern individual biography.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably The Doctrine of the Mean and Mencius), sincerity is framed through Confucianism and Cynicism. Some passages define sincerity; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through sincerity, god, humanity.

Concepts in this quote

Sincerity
Sincerity appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat sincerity as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
God
God appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat god as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Humanity
Humanity names both the species and the moral quality of being humane—bridging anthropology and ethics.
